headline: Shorts collapsed 8× in 3 weeks: views/short went from ~566 (Aug 2–7) to ~70 (Aug 20–24) and total daily channel views crashed from 1,401 (Aug 7) to 64 (Aug 24) — a ~22× drop. Impressions per short fell ~60% and the algorithm stopped pushing Ep 11's long-form: 1,090 impressions at 6 days in vs Ep 10's 5,908 (5.4× less push). SHORTS drove 87% of channel views for the last 73 days (16,842 of ~19,391); when the shorts feed died, the channel died. The single biggest lever is the funnel: SHORTS_CONTENT_LINKS shows 5 lifetime views — the pinned-comment + related-video + end-screen wiring has been unrun for 4+ episodes and Aug 20–25's best-AVD shorts (100–158% replay) got 2–43 impressions each. Fix the funnel first, then match the hook pool back to what actually landed (money/greed/gambling, not earnest explainers).

production.title: The shorts funnel is dead — SHORTS_CONTENT_LINKS = 5 lifetime views; wire it for every Ep 11 short before shifting anything else
production.evidence: Traffic-source lifetime: SHORTS feed 16,842 views (87% of channel) vs SHORTS_CONTENT_LINKS 5 views (0.026%). Aug 20–24 shorts with 100–158% AVD (Harambe 158%, Dog cancer $3k 142%, Ride to zero 291% earlier) each got 2–61 impressions — the algorithm found the retention winners and there's still no click path to long-form. The funnel checklist has been logged as owed in memory since Ep 7 (four episodes running). Ep 11 shorts publishing daily 8/22–8/28.
production.recommendation: Block 30 min today: on each of the 6 already-live Ep 11 shorts + the 3 scheduled 8/26–28, (1) pin comment with episode URL + timestamped moment (`youtu.be/yooe89JxPo4?t=NNN`), (2) set a related-video override to Ep 11, (3) confirm end-screen CTAs point to Ep 11 or the channel. Do it live in Studio, then set a durable rule: uploader script prints a funnel checklist per Ep, and it doesn't get closed until every short in the batch is wired.
production.status_note: same fix has been open since Ep 7 memory; the data now shows it as the top-return lever this week

production.title: Hook pool drifted from money/greed to earnest explainers — match what actually landed
production.evidence: Aug 2–7 winners (4-digit views): 'Make me a millionaire' 1,214v · 'The baby egg allergy test' 1,148v · 'He rolled dice 100 times to protect his Bitcoin' 987v · 'Thank you Jito for sponsoring' 865v · 'Claude don't cut this out' 728v. Aug 20–25 shorts topped out at 175v ('Gorilla mode, explained badly'), median 36v. The Aug 2–7 winners are money-lever, gambling, degen-behavior one-liners; the Aug 20–25 pool is 'sloppy migration explainer,' 'AI safety,' 'cured his dog's cancer' — earnest and topical. AVD is fine on both windows (~50–150%); the difference is hook shape, not delivery.
production.recommendation: For Ep 12 clip picks: bias 4-of-7 shorts to money/greed/gambling hooks — DOGE max long, the LIT report card ('the AI longed Hyperliquid's competitor ON Hyperliquid'), the perp P&L one-liners, the apology-trial/100× wallet-funding bits. Save earnest/explainer picks (GLM-5.3, mind-viruses, Coldcard 14-month) for the 3 slots where the writing IS the punchline.

production.title: Ep 11 lost the algorithm push — 1,090 impressions at 6 days vs Ep 10's 5,908; the retro-fix window is closing
production.evidence: Ep 10 (8/14): 5,908 impressions, 0.49% CTR (worst-ever launch, per Ep 10 memory; degraded further from initial 0.61%). Ep 11 (8/20, 6 days old at pull): 1,090 impressions, 1.56% CTR. Ep 11's CTR is 3× Ep 10's but on 5.4× less impressions — YouTube is not pushing the video. Historical anchor: ~95% of a video's lifetime impressions arrive in the first 7 days (memory: analytics-measurement-traps).
production.recommendation: Same-day: re-shrink-test Ep 11 thumbnail on the mobile feed (memory says it passed initially, but the 1,090-imp trajectory suggests it isn't converting the tiny push it got). Consider a title A/B: current 'Did AI Just Cure Cancer? The $3,000 Dog Vaccine Story' vs a punchier draft (segment-times.md has 4 alternates). Do not retitle mid-flight without a segment-times.md log line (Ep 10 did this and it made the packaging debug impossible).

production.title: Shorts scheduled 8/26–28 will ride the collapse — consider swapping ordering or rescheduling as a burst
production.evidence: Scheduled: 8/26 'Please don't deport me, Brian' · 8/27 'Three AIs, zero knew what we bought' · 8/28 'The Banks Should Spy on You Act.' production.recommendation: Either (a) resequence: put 'Three AIs, zero knew what we bought' first — it's the closest to a money-lever hook — and hold Brian for a moment with prior-context lift; (b) burst-publish all three within 6 h on the same day (see if the algorithm re-engages on volume) as an explicit experiment. Log the choice.

production.title: Channel is losing subs — net −1 over 30 days (3 gained, 4 lost); 3 lost in a single day (8/19)
production.evidence: Daily sub deltas over the pull window: gained on 8/4 (+1), 8/11 (+1), 8/14 (+1); lost on 8/14 (−1), 8/19 (−3). Net −1 over 30 days. The 8/19 spike coincides with the day before Ep 11 dropped — subs bailed on Ep 10's aftermath (which had the worst-ever CTR + undocumented retitle). Sub gains from shorts: essentially zero across the entire 30-day window despite ~7,000 shorts views.
production.recommendation: Investigate whether the branded ender added in Ep 10 is landing (channel-name visible? sub CTA readable?). If not, the ender is a UI change with no measurable conversion — worth iterating. Also: pinned-comment fix from item #1 above is the same lever (shorts viewers with no click path never become subs).

recording.title: Ep 11 cold open didn't hold — 30% at 5%, drops to 13% at end; vs_typical 0.19–0.34 (well below channel-genre norm)
recording.evidence: Retention @ 5%: 30% (vs_typical 0.19) · 10%: 23% (vs_typical 0.34) · 15–20%: 20% (vs_typical 0.27–0.31) · 30–50%: 16.7% (vs_typical 0.50–0.72) · 75–100%: 13% (vs_typical 0.44–0.53). The 5–10% window (roughly 2:30–5:00 of the 49:25 cut) is where the leak concentrates — that's post-cold-open, into the check-in / first real segment. vs_typical <0.35 in the first 20% means viewers who WOULD normally hold on a similar video are still bailing on this one.
recording.recommendation: The cold open ≤60s rule is holding structurally; the failure is that the tease at :51 doesn't fund what starts at 2:30. Two record-side fixes for Ep 12: (a) after the ≤60s cold open, don't drop back into H (check-ins) — bank the perp reveal + a tease of the marquee (A) BEFORE H. Check-ins at :51 is a decel that vs_typical proves is worse than genre norm. (b) The tease itself needs a stakes line — Ep 11's cold open was strong on hook but light on 'here's what you'll know by the end'; try one sentence of finale-promise.

recording.title: Shorts drive 87% of views but 0 subs — hosts need to name the show + say 'subscribe' inside the short
recording.evidence: SHORTS traffic source: 16,842 views (87% of channel lifetime). Subs gained in the 30-day window with shorts running daily: 3 (net −1). Comparing to earlier eras — the 7/20 short 'The AI's trade broke $10 live mid-show' drove +1 sub on 449 views; recent shorts drove +1 sub across ~7,000 shorts views in the last week. The branded ender added in Ep 10 is visible but no on-mic CTA runs inside the shorts themselves.
recording.recommendation: In every Ep 12 recording, land ONE line per segment that would clip as a self-contained short AND identifies the show. E.g. 'On Permanent Underpod this week, our AI longed Hyperliquid's rival ON Hyperliquid.' Names the show inside the clippable moment — no post-edit CTA needed. This is a discipline change more than a script change: hosts already do the moments, they just don't brand them.

recording.title: The money/greed/gambling hook pool is where subs get earned — build more of it into the show, not just the perp segment
recording.evidence: The 4-digit shorts of the Aug 2–7 peak all came from money/degen moments: 'Make me a millionaire' (Ep 8 perp), 'CRISPR agent, built different' (Ep 8 T-shirt bit), 'dice 100 times to protect Bitcoin' (Ep 8 Coldcard), 'Sandwich bot' (Ep 6 finale). Those hooks are Chris's + Tyler's segments as much as Jackson's perp — they emerged when EACH segment had a money-lever punchline. Aug 14–25 shorts are all explainer-flavored; the show got structurally more earnest between Ep 9 and Ep 11.
recording.recommendation: Standing recording note: in every non-perp segment, land at least one 'the number that shocks' or 'the trade that broke' or 'the greed that failed' one-liner. GLM-5.3 has one built-in ('coherent plans for complete exploitation chains'); the Coldcard 14-month warning has one ('14 months ignored, $116M gone'). Don't leave them to the edit — name them on mic.

recording.title: The perp-rides-all-episode format keeps validating; keep it structural for Ep 12
recording.evidence: Ep 10 memory notes 'best-ever ending validates perp-rides-all-episode'; Ep 11 board closed −$16 (from Ep 10's −$36) — the arc holds. Ep 11's retention at ratio 1.0 is 13.3% with vs_typical 0.53 (BEST vs_typical marker on the whole curve, alongside the 60% mark's 0.17). The finale over-indexes vs channel norms because there's a promised reveal.
recording.recommendation: Ep 12's F (DOGE max long, Pitcoin bit) already opens the pip and rides to a live close on the end card. Keep that structural. If Warsh's Jackson Hole quote (Topic W) lands late enough to be the second finale beat, thread the perp reveal INTO Warsh — not before or after — to double-anchor the last 3 minutes.
